# Packet — ani-125-rubric: Spell 125 — the rubric

Established from Budge 1895, pp. 222–224. Start: {"page": 222, "plate": "XXXIII", "line": 1, "note": "Under the heading PLATE XXXIII: 'àn Àusàr Ani maāχeru' (See Osiris Ani, triumphant); àn and unχ - f … θàb overlined (red)."}. End: {"page": 224, "plate": "XXXIII", "line": 10, "lastWord": "sep", "note": "... in unbroken regularity, millions of times. (immediately above the short rule and the heading 'Appendix.')"}.
Left out as not Ani's text: p. 222: footnote 1, a 'less corrupt text' of lines 1–4 printed in hieroglyphs from Naville, Todtenbuch Bd. II, Bl. 332; p. 223: footnotes 1–4, variant spellings (sekertu; 'pigs and donkeys'; 'satisfying the heart of the king and of his nobles'; 'shall be given to him bread, vessels of drink, cakes'); p. 224: the section headed 'Appendix.' (from Naville, Todtenbuch Bd. I, Bl. 140) and its footnote.

One line per word of the established text, in order: index · page/plate/line · signs (code=character, * = not yet in the sign glossary: add it with signs.py before building) · layout · Budge's transliteration · Budge's English (his 1895 understanding: a check on sense, never wording) · flags.
Your units must use these signs in exactly this order (the build compares the whole sequence); you may join or split Budge's word groups where the grammar requires (say so in the note when you do).
